subject: Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit — Finsolve discovery (next steps)
preview: Recap from today's discovery on Dedicated capacity: pain points, success criteria, throughput targets, and next steps (PoC + SOW).
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@finsolve.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:35:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit — Finsolve discovery (next steps)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move toward a PoC / sizing:

What we heard (pain points)
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak trading windows leading to degraded UX for your analytics customers.
- Current self-hosted stack (GCP, custom autoscaler) struggles with cold KV-cache and causes 95/99 latency spikes.
- Unit token costs are rising as you scale; you want a predictable cost model.
- Compliance: need VPC isolation + KMS-managed keys + SOC2 evidence for audits.

Current stack / constraints you shared
- Models hosted in-house on GCP (mixture of float32 and int8 quantized), run on 8x A100 ephemeral instances.
- Average traffic baseline ~400 TPS sustained for inference routes; spikes to ~700-800 TPS for 10–15m windows.
- Cannot accept noisy neighbors on inference workloads; need reserved capacity for critical routes.

Success criteria for a Dedicated offering
- Predictable p95 latency <150ms on core routes and stable p99 behavior during bursts.
- 99.9% uptime SLA and isolation (dedicated GPU pool + optional VPC).
- Baseline throughput support 400 TPS with ability to burst to 800 TPS for short windows.
- Integrations: KMS for key management, audit logs delivered for SOC2 scope.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to provide sizing + short proposal (attached: finsolve-dedicated-recap-20260318.pdf).
2) Draft SOW for a 2-week PoC to validate latency/throughput and integration items (attached: rd-sow-draft-v1.pdf).
3) Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra/ML infra team + our Solutions Engineer (30–45m).
4) Provide required audit/log export list for your compliance team (we listed the typical items in the attachment).

Questions for you / to confirm
- Is the 400 TPS baseline correct for all inference routes or only for the primary analytics route?
- Do you have existing preferred time windows for the 2-week PoC kickoff (we can start as early as 04/05)?

If that aligns, I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineer and draft the PoC success criteria (latency targets, test harness, sample load profile).

Thanks again — great conversation.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated Capacity fit — Finsolve discovery (next steps)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Couple quick clarifications: 

- Baseline TPS: the 400 TPS is for the primary analytics route only. Secondary routes are ~60–80 TPS each. Total sustained across all routes ~560 TPS.
- Spikes: those 700–800 TPS spikes are typically concentrated on the primary route during market opens; they last ~10–15 minutes.
- Compliance: yes, SOC2 + proof of KMS integration required. We also need encrypted request logs stored for 90 days.

Two asks before we sign off on the PoC plan:
1) Can you outline how Redwood’s autoscaling interacts with reserved GPU pools? Specifically: how quickly can you scale up for bursts and what controls exist to bound cost?
2) Pricing: what’s the incremental cost for burst capacity above the reserved baseline, and is there a hard cap option?

If you can share those details and the proposed PoC start window (04/05 works for us tentatively), we’ll lock in resources on our side.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Finsolve
j.ellis@finsolve.com

Jordan —

Great, thanks for the clarifications — that helps. Quick answers to your two asks below and next steps: 

1) Autoscaling + reserved pools
- Reserved GPU pools provide baseline capacity guaranteed to your tenant (we isolate the pool). Autoscaling for bursts is handled by attaching burstable capacity on top of the reserved pool.
- Scale-up latency: warm scaling (using pre-warmed standby instances) typically <60s; cold scale-ups (spinning new instances) can be 3–7 minutes depending on instance type and region.
- Bounding cost: we offer a configurable burst cap (percentage above baseline, e.g., 50–100%) and a hard spend cap option. We can set alerts and automated fallback to a cheaper model variant if burst thresholds exceed the cap.

2) Burst pricing and caps
- Typical structure we propose for Dedicated: base reserved fee (capacity + SLA) + metered burst usage. For a customer with Finsolve's profile we'd model bursts as metered at an incremental rate (example: 1.4x of the unit token rate for burst tokens) with an optional hard cap. Exact numbers depend on final sizing; I’ll include a sample pricing table in the formal proposal.

Next steps (action items)
- I’ll send an updated SOW + sample pricing matrix by EOD tomorrow and add explicit PoC success criteria (p95/p99 targets, test harness).
- Vanessa (cc) — can you and the Solutions Engineering team join a 30–45m technical deep-dive? Proposed slots: Thu 03/25 10:00am PT, Fri 03/26 9:00am PT, Mon 03/29 11:00am PT.
- Jordan — can you confirm PoC kickoff week tentatively starting 04/05?

If that all looks good I’ll create the HubSpot deal and draft the formal docs.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
